items.title: Strong Wolfe counterexample
items.statement:
\label{thm:main}
For every $0<c_1<2/3$ and $2/3\le c_2<1$, there exist
$f\in C^2(\R^2)$, $x_0\in\R^2$, $H_0\succ0$, and a sequence of positive
step lengths such that
$\frac12I\preceq\nabla^2f(x)\preceq\frac32I$ for all $x$, and the
classical DFP sequence satisfies the standard strong Wolfe conditions
at every iteration but $\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\to1$.
The Hessian is globally $1/2$-H\"older continuous and has no H\"older
bound of exponent $\beta\in(1/2,1]$ on the initial level set.
These conclusions hold in every dimension $n\ge2$.

theorem planarCounterexampleFamilyWithSequenceProperties (c₁ c₂ : ℝ)
    (hc₁ : 0 < c₁) (hc₁lim : c₁ < 2 / 3) (hc₂lim : 2 / 3 ≤ c₂) (hc₂ : c₂ < 1) :
    ∃ νStar > baseAngle, ∃ κ > 0, ∃ Cgrad > 0, ∃ lower > 0, ∃ upper > 0,
      ∃ productLower > 0, ∃ productUpper > 0,
      ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ε < 1 → ∃ J : ℕ, 0 < J ∧ ∀ j₀ ≥ J,
        ∃ w : DFP.StrongWolfeCounterexample (Fin 2) (1 / 2) (3 / 2) c₁ c₂,
          PlanarCounterexample.SourceIdentity (Parameters.of j₀ νStar) κ w ∧
          PlanarCounterexample.CounterexampleProperties ε w ∧
          SequenceProperties.SourceEstimates (Parameters.of j₀ νStar) νStar
            Cgrad lower upper productLower productUpper := by
  obtain ⟨ηs, hηs, hsourceData⟩ := PlanarCounterexample.sourceDataNeighborhood
  obtain ⟨ηq, hηq, hsequenceData⟩ := SequenceProperties.sourceSequenceNeighborhood
  obtain ⟨νStar, hνStar, _, Jw, _, hmodels⟩ :=
    WolfeRatios.existsUniformModelWolfe c₁ c₂ (min ηs ηq) hc₁ hc₁lim hc₂lim hc₂ (lt_min hηs hηq)
  have hnearSource : νStar ∈ Set.Ioo baseAngle (baseAngle + ηs) :=
    Set.Ioo_subset_Ioo_right (add_le_add le_rfl (min_le_left ηs ηq)) hνStar
  have hnearSequence : νStar ∈ Set.Ioo baseAngle (baseAngle + ηq) :=
    Set.Ioo_subset_Ioo_right (add_le_add le_rfl (min_le_right ηs ηq)) hνStar
  obtain ⟨κ, hκ, C, _, H, hH, haccuracy⟩ := hsourceData νStar hnearSource
  obtain ⟨Cgrad, hCgrad, lower, hlower, upper, hupper, productLower, hProductLower,
    productUpper, hProductUpper, Jq, _, hsequences⟩ := hsequenceData νStar hnearSequence
  refine ⟨νStar, hνStar.1, κ, hκ, Cgrad, hCgrad, lower, hlower, upper, hupper,
    productLower, hProductLower, productUpper, hProductUpper, ?_⟩
  intro ε hε _
  let δ := min ε (1 / 2)
  have hhalf : (0 : ℝ) < 1 / 2 := by norm_num
  have hhalfOne : (1 / 2 : ℝ) < 1 := by norm_num
  have hδ : 0 < δ := lt_min hε hhalf
  have hδhalf : δ ≤ 1 / 2 := min_le_right _ _
  have hδε : δ ≤ ε := min_le_left _ _
  have hδone : δ < 1 := hδhalf.trans_lt hhalfOne
  obtain ⟨Js, hJs, hsource⟩ := haccuracy δ hδ hδone
  refine ⟨max Js (max Jw Jq), hJs.trans_le (le_max_left _ _), ?_⟩
  intro j₀ hj₀
  have hjSource : Js ≤ j₀ := (le_max_left _ _).trans hj₀
  have hjWolfe : Jw ≤ j₀ := ((le_max_left _ _).trans (le_max_right _ _)).trans hj₀
  have hjSequence : Jq ≤ j₀ := ((le_max_right _ _).trans (le_max_right _ _)).trans hj₀
  have hactual := hsource j₀ hjSource
  have hwolfe := SequenceProperties.strongWolfeOfSourceModel hactual.objective
    hc₁ (hc₁lim.trans_le hc₂lim) hc₂ (hmodels j₀ hjWolfe)
  obtain ⟨w, hidentity, hproperties⟩ :=
    PlanarCounterexample.certificateOfSourceData hactual hδhalf hδε hH.le hwolfe
  exact ⟨w, hidentity, hproperties, hsequences j₀ hjSequence⟩

  obtain ⟨Kturn, hKturn, Jt, _, hturns⟩ := hturnData νStar hnearTurn
  refine ⟨νStar, hνStar.1, κ, hκ, Cgrad, hCgrad, lower, hlower, upper, hupper,

  intro ε hε _

  refine ⟨max Js (max Jw (max Jq Jt)), hJs.trans_le (le_max_left _ _), ?_⟩

    ((le_max_left _ _).trans ((le_max_right _ _).trans (le_max_right _ _))).trans hj₀

    ((le_max_right _ _).trans ((le_max_right _ _).trans (le_max_right _ _))).trans hj₀

items.label: Corollary 2
items.title: Identity initialization
items.statement:
\label{cor:identity-initialization}
For every parameter pair in Theorem~\ref{thm:main} and every
$n\ge2$, a strongly convex objective function
$\widetilde f\in C^2(\R^n)$ with globally $1/2$-H\"older continuous
Hessian admits an infinite classical DFP sequence initialized with
$\widetilde H_0=I$, satisfying the standard strong Wolfe conditions and
$\liminf_k\|\nabla\widetilde f(\widetilde x_k)\|>0$.
The origin is its unique minimizer, $\widetilde f(0)=0$, and its Hessian
has positive global lower and upper bounds that may depend on the
example. The accumulation set is an ellipse centered at the origin
in a two-dimensional subspace.

theorem identityInitializationExplicit (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (c₁ c₂ : ℝ)
    (hc₁ : 0 < c₁) (hc₁lim : c₁ < 2 / 3) (hc₂lim : 2 / 3 ≤ c₂) (hc₂ : c₂ < 1) :
    ∃ m M : ℝ, 0 < m ∧ 0 < M ∧ m ≤ M ∧
      ∃ it : DFP.InverseIteration (Fin n),
        ContDiff ℝ 2 it.objective ∧ StrongConvexOn Set.univ m it.objective ∧
          HasHessianBounds m M it.objective ∧
          it.inverseHessian 0 = (1 : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℝ) ∧
          (∀ k, 0 < it.stepLength k) ∧
          (∀ k, LineSearch.IsStrongWolfe c₁ c₂ it.objective
            (it.point k) (it.point (k + 1) - it.point k)) ∧
          0 < liminf (fun k ↦ ‖DFP.gradients it.objective it.point k‖) atTop ∧
          ∃ i : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) →ₗ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n),
            Function.Injective i ∧ Module.finrank ℝ (LinearMap.range i) = 2 ∧
              {x | MapClusterPt x atTop it.point} = i '' Metric.sphere 0 1 ∧
              (∃ C > 0, ∀ x y, ‖hessian it.objective x - hessian it.objective y‖ ≤
                C * ‖x - y‖ ^ (1 / 2 : ℝ)) ∧
              it.objective 0 = 0 ∧
              ∀ x, (∀ y, it.objective x ≤ it.objective y) ↔ x = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨m, M, hm, hM, hmM, d, hconvex, i, hproperties⟩ :=
    identityInitialization n hn c₁ c₂ hc₁ hc₁lim hc₂lim hc₂
  exact ⟨m, M, hm, hM, hmM, d.iteration, d.objectiveContDiff, hconvex,
    d.hessianBounds, d.initialInverseHessian_eq_one, d.stepLengthPos, d.strongWolfe,
    d.gradientNormLiminfPos, i, hproperties.injective, hproperties.range_finrank,
    hproperties.cluster, hproperties.half_holder, hproperties.origin,
    hproperties.unique_minimizer⟩

\label{thm:planar-convergence}
Let $f\in C^2(\R^2)$ satisfy $\nabla^2f(x)\succeq\mu I$ for all
$x\in\R^2$ and some $\mu>0$. Let $x_0\in\R^2$ and $H_0\succ0$
be arbitrary, and fix $0<c_1<c_2<1$. Suppose $\nabla^2f$ is locally
Lipschitz continuous on a neighborhood of the initial level set
$K=\{x\in\R^2:f(x)\le f(x_0)\}$.
Then classical DFP with update \eqref{eq:dfp-update} and positive step
lengths satisfying \eqref{eq:armijo} and \eqref{eq:weak-curvature}
either reaches the unique minimizer $x_*$ in finitely many iterations or
generates an infinite sequence satisfying
$x_k\longrightarrow x_*$ and $\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\longrightarrow0$.

\label{lem:planar-degeneration}
Let $f\in C^2(\R^2)$ be $\mu$-strongly convex, where $\mu>0$.
Consider an infinite sequence of nonstationary iterates with
$g_k=\nabla f(x_k)$, $s_k=-\alpha_kH_kg_k$,
$x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k$, and $y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k$, where $H_k\succ0$,
$\alpha_k>0$, and every step satisfies \eqref{eq:armijo} and
\eqref{eq:weak-curvature} for fixed $0<c_1<c_2<1$.
Suppose $H_ky_{k-1}=s_{k-1}$ for $k\ge1$. Put
\begin{equation}\label{eq:planar-scalar-definition}
\ell_k=\|s_k\|,\qquad
\kappa_k=\frac{s_k^Ty_k}{\ell_k^2},\qquad
\lambda_k=\kappa_{k-1}\det H_k\quad(k\ge1).
\end{equation}
If $x_k$ does not converge to the unique minimizer $x_*$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:planar-degeneration}
0<\lambda_k\le C\ell_{k-1}\ell_k\longrightarrow0
\end{equation}
for all sufficiently large $k$, with $C$ independent of $k$.
Moreover, $\{H_k\}$ is bounded and $\lambda_{\min}(H_k)\to0$.
